**My thinking, as this farmer:**

I have been working this land since I was a girl. My mother grew wheat and corn, and her mother before her. In Quzhou, that is what the land is for — the soil is flat and deep, the wells are there, the wheat buyer comes every June. I don't need a book to tell me what to do.

My household has about 8 mu of contracted land. I will plant all of it to winter wheat this autumn, then turn it straight to summer corn after harvest — same as every year. I buy seeds from Old Liu's shop in the village. He sells the hybrid corn everyone uses now, and the wheat seed the township recommends. I trust what works.

For fertilizer, I put down diammonium phosphate and urea. I maybe use a bit more urea than some, because I worry about thin stalks. My neighbors do the same. I irrigate from the village well — wheat needs water before it goes dormant, again in spring when it shoots up, and once more when the heads fill. Corn I water less. I spray for weeds in wheat and watch for armyworm in corn.

I do not try new things I don't understand. I am 50, my back hurts, and I manage this land mostly alone since my husband works in the city. I do what I know.
